name: cloudy-all-go-mcp
description: Go port of cloudy-all-mcp (fleet MCP router: list_servers, list_tools, call over stateless Streamable HTTP, mesh-first with public bearer fallback, 60 s tool cache), shadow stage: runs next to the TypeScript container on its own port and container, outside every request path (ticket #1874)

native_build._doc: Same multi-stage template as c3bot-relay-go (#1873): compiled in golang on the arch-matched runner (oci-apps is arm64), shipped as one static binary on distroless static nonroot (CA bundle for the public https route). golang:1.25 because modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk requires go 1.25.

api.description: Same contract as cloudy-all-mcp: stateless Streamable HTTP POST /mcp with tools list_servers, list_tools, call; GET /health.

mcp.description: Fleet MCP router (3 tools), Go port.

parity-compare._doc: Reference = the TypeScript router (infra-api_cloudy-all-mcp/src/code, node type stripping) run next to the Go router in front of one fake child MCP; the same 40 requests go to both and the normalised responses must be identical. See parity/parity_test.go.

parity-mutation.cmd: o=$(mktemp); PARITY_MUTATE=1 PARITY_REQUIRE=1 go test -count=1 -tags parity -run TestParity ./parity/ >"$o" 2>&1; grep -q 'steps differ' "$o"
parity-mutation._doc: Mutation proof: the Go router is made to change one tool description; the parity harness must go red (the grep passes only if it reported differing steps, not on a build error).

_doc_shadow: Shadow stage (#1874). The live TypeScript router (container cloudy-all-mcp, port 3112) is untouched. This container has no env_file and no secret, so it reaches the child MCPs over their mesh endpoints only; nothing outside the host dials it. Switch-over (the real secret, mesh name cloudy-all-mcp, Caddy route) is a separate step after the live comparison; the TypeScript image stays declared for one release as the rollback.
